'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***At least 24 people are killed and 55 injured after [[Sudan]]'s [[Rapid Support Forces]] [[Shell (projectile)|shell]] residential areas of [[Al-Fashir]], [[North Darfur]]. The city remains under siege as the last military stronghold in [[Darfur|the region]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sudan-military-rsf-darfur-el-fasher-d5f8bb5589f1c77b95c107bd72d15449 (AP)]
*[[Afghanistan–Pakistan clashes (2024–present)|Afghanistan–Pakistan clashes]]

'''Health and environment'''

**[[Denmark|Danish]] [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Denmark)|foreign minister]] [[Lars Løkke Rasmussen]] summons the [[U.S.]] [[chargé d'affaires]] in [[Copenhagen]] after individuals linked to [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] conducted [[Covert operation|covert influence activities]] in [[Greenland]]. '''Law and crime'''
*[[Mass shootings in the United States]]
**[[Annunciation Catholic Church shooting]]
***Two people are killed and 18 more injured, including at least four critically, in a [[mass shooting]] at the Annunciation Church in [[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]], [[United States]] in an alleged [[Anti-Catholicism in the United States|anti-Catholic]] hate crime. The suspect died by [[suicide]] at the scene. [https://bnonews.com/index.php/2025/08/active-shooter-at-annunciation-church-in-minneapolis/ (BNO News)] [https://knsiradio.com/2025/08/27/multiple-casualties-reported-at-minneapolis-church/ (KNSI-AM)]
*[[Assassination of Miguel Uribe Turbay]]
**A [[Colombia]]n [[Judiciary of Colombia|court]] sentences a 15-year-old to seven years in [[Juvenile delinquency|juvenile detention]] for [[Attempted murder|attempted]] [[Crime in Colombia#Murder|murder]] and [[criminal possession of a weapon]] in connection with the assassination of [[Senate of Colombia|Senator]] [[Miguel Uribe Turbay]] in June. [https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20250828-teen-shooter-colombia-miguel-uribe (France 24)]
*A [[Bolivia]]n [[Judiciary of Bolivia|court]] grants [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]] leader [[Luis Fernando Camacho]]'s transfer to [[house arrest]] after more than two years in [[pre-trial detention]], allowing him to resume his duties as [[Governor of Santa Cruz Department|Governor]] of [[Santa Cruz Department|Santa Cruz]] while still facing trial on charges related to the [[2019 Bolivian political crisis|2019 political unrest]] and a [[2022 in Bolivia|2022 strike]]. [https://apnews.com/article/bolivia-evo-morales-luis-fernando-camacho-jail-872ae180aeb8a23eedf306f3f9e940ef (AP)]
*A [[Morocco|Moroccan]] [[Judiciary of Morocco|court]] rejects a request to provisionally release [[Human rights in Morocco|human rights]] activist [[Ibtissame Lachgar]], who faces [[Blasphemy law|blasphemy charges]] for online content while experiencing serious illness. [https://apnews.com/article/morocco-blasphemy-trial-lesbian-fdc38b2d491ae2c0ec3b6c565b3d3d9b (AP)]
*A [[South Africa]]n [[Promotion of Equality and Prevention of Unfair Discrimination Act, 2000|equality court]] finds [[Limpopo]] [[National Assembly of South Africa|representative]] and leader of the second-largest opposition party [[Julius Malema]] guilty of [[hate speech]] over remarks made at a 2022 rally, where he encouraged violence in the context of [[Riot|revolution]]. [https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-race-white-trump-malema-aade286269e02e8e85a1394ea2e74d66 (AP)]

**[[Philippine]] [[President of the Philippines|president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] orders lifestyle checks on [[Government of the Philippines|government]] officials, beginning with the [[Department of Public Works and Highways]], as part of an investigation into alleged [[Corruption in the Philippines|corruption]] in [[flood control]] projects that have received [[Philippine peso|₱]]545 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]9.5 billion) in funding since 2022.
